segments: and Sibylla {OCR?}, the queen, together with her male and female servants and the eunuchs that she had, and all her possessions;
and he sent horsemen with her, who brought her to the border of the Franks.
And also the other Frankish noblewomen who were present in Jerusalem,
he sent away in peace with their possessions.
And the Patriarch also took out with him all the treasures of the Church of the Resurrection and of the rest of the churches—the lamps of gold and of silver, and so forth.
And the people of the city likewise, whatever they were unable to carry,
they were selling to one another.
And in brief,
empty of all provisions, they surrendered Jerusalem to the Arabs.
A certain secretary named Imad said to Saladin:
"Why should they take out all this wealth, when you gave your word for their lives alone?"
And Saladin said:
"It is true,
but the Franks do not understand [it thus];
and if we withhold their possessions,
they will spread the report against us that we swore an oath and lied,
and they will bring an evil name upon us."
Now Saladin took control over Jerusalem on Friday, the 27th
of their seventh month, in the year
583 of the Arabs,
which is the twelfth of First Tishri, in the year 1498
1498 of the Greeks (1187 of our Lord?);
after 28
days from the conjunction of the six wandering stars [planets].
And from this time the Christians no longer held sway over Jerusalem,
except that the same Saladin left four Frankish monks in the Church of the Resurrection,
so that they might minister at the Holy Sepulchre.
And after a little while,
the Patriarch of the Greeks took charge of the administration of that same church.
And when Saladin had finished with Jerusalem,
he went and encamped against Tyre, which sits in the heart of the sea;
and he built strong towers {OCR?} against it.
And he directed all the might of his battle against Tyre,
and he urged on all his forces {OCR?}, saying:
"The Franks have nowhere left to lay their head on the sea-coast
except Tyre;
and when we take this,
their hope of sending forth an expedition will be cut off,
and we shall be at ease from them."
And with such words they were sharpening {OCR?} their stings.
However, because the Marquis, who had come from Rome, had fortified it well with provisions and stout-hearted men,
the Franks were continually making sorties,
and they were killing the Arabs and retreating inside;
